cases.why: A member whose value references a member declared LATER in the same enum. VB6 compiles the whole module before running it, so order need not matter to it - but it decides everything for a pre-pass that walks in source order. If forward references are legal the evaluation must be lazy or two-pass; if illegal, a single forward walk is sufficient and much simpler.
A member value reaching into a DIFFERENT enum by qualified name. Decides whether enum resolution is per-enum or program-wide, and whether the pre-pass can finish one enum before starting the next.

The same-enum reference written in QUALIFIED form, while the enum is still being declared. The bare form is measured legal; this asks whether the enum's own name is in scope inside its own body, which a naive implementation would get wrong in either direction.

A member referencing a Const declared AFTER the enum. The forward-Const case is what separates 'evaluate during a source-order walk' from 'evaluate lazily'; CLAUDE.md names order-independent Const evaluation as the reason the lazy-memoised pattern exists at all, so this is the case that says whether enums need it too.
